findings.mechanism: Static field `latest` points to the newest RequestContext, and each context holds a `previous` reference to the one before it (set in open(), line ~26). Nothing ever clears it, so every context ever created, with its 384-byte padded body byte[], caller/path strings, is reachable from the static root as one unbounded linked list.
findings.cause: previous-request link kept only to log previousPath() and microsSincePrevious() in the audit line; it needs just the prior path and arrival time (two scalars), not the whole prior context. Fix: store previousPath and previousReceivedAt as values, and don't keep the previous object (or the body).
findings.evidence: Ran gateway.Main 20000 (System.gc() before each checkpoint): heap in use 4431 KB @5000, 6556 @10000, 9042 @15000, 11507 @20000 requests, i.e. about 0.45 KB per request, linear in requests served, even after full GC.

findings.mechanism: Per-account history deques and balances maps are long-lived fields.
findings.evidence: Code review: note() trims each deque to HISTORY_PER_ACCOUNT=20 and the maps are keyed by a fixed set of 64 accounts (transfer/balance don't add keys); the heap growth measured matches the RequestContext chain.
findings.discriminator: History is capped at 20 entries per account and the key set is fixed, so the size is bounded regardless of request count.

findings.mechanism: Gateway routes map and audit sink (the Main sink only increments counters, doesn't store lines).
findings.evidence: Code review: routes is filled once in the constructor with 3 entries; `served` is an int; Main's sink keeps two long counters, not the lines.
findings.discriminator: Routes are fixed at 3 entries and the audit sink retains no lines, so nothing here grows per request.
